findings.title: [Contract deviation, confirmed] Home-profile PDF page is not the sheet: MediaBox is 262 x 210 mm for poche on A4, not A4 landscape
findings.where: /home/user/ebook-cadeau/crates/ebc-layout/src/page.rs:95-110 and 160-163 (page_geometry / new_page); root cause in /home/user/ebook-cadeau/crates/ebc-scene/src/document.rs:330-367 (single scalar Page::slug) and /home/user/ebook-cadeau/crates/ebc-pdf/src/writer.rs:202-219
findings.evidence: Contract (architecture.md:253-254): 'For home profiles the PDF page IS the sheet (MediaBox = A4 landscape ...)'. I wrote the pages through ebc-pdf from a scratch crate and ran `pdfinfo -box`: poche/home_a4 -> 'Page size: 742.677 x 595.276 pts' (262 x 210 mm; A4 landscape is 841.89 x 595.28); poche/home_letter -> 759.40 x 612.00 (267.9 x 215.9; Letter is 792 x 612); a6/home_letter -> media 279.4 x 207.4. No named preset on any named sheet gets media_is_sheet = true. The crate's own tests pin the deviation instead of the contract (page::tests::poche_on_a4_is_centred_and_full_height asserts `!s.media_is_sheet` and media 262 x 210; tests/invariants.rs:301-306 only requires the media to fill the sheet 'in one direction at least'). Two sparring tests that appeared during the audit fail on exactly this: tests/spar_contract.rs::home_a4_page_is_a4_landscape and ::home_media_box_is_the_sheet_for_every_preset_that_fits. The rustdoc at page.rs:151-153 states as fact that 'a PDF viewer centres the page on the paper, which gives the same result' although the implementer's report says this was never tested. Domain consequence: registration of the two sides now depends on the viewer/driver centring an off-size page. If it anchors the page top-left instead, side 1 sits 17.5 mm off centre and, after the sheet is turned, side 2 sits 17.5 mm off the other way: 35 mm front/back misregistration (poche on A4). Off-size pages also provoke paper-size-mismatch prompts on some drivers. The implementer reported this deviation honestly; the report is accurate.
findings.suggested_fix: Cross-crate: give ebc_scene::Page an explicit media box (e.g. `media: Option<Rect>` in page coordinates, or per-side slug [left, top, right, bottom]); make ebc-pdf's page_boxes write MediaBox = CropBox from it and offset Bleed/TrimBox accordingly; then new_page sets it from SheetPlacement::sheet (already computed). Replace the tests that assert `!media_is_sheet` with one asserting media == sheet for every home preset, and drop the unverified 'viewer centres the page' sentence. Mark reach can then be per axis instead of min(mx, my).

findings.title: [Domain error] Fold marks are drawn as solid ticks identical to crop marks; on the press profile the top/bottom edges read exactly like a 2-up with a 10 mm gutter
findings.evidence: fold_marks(poche, professional_eu) returns one stroke with empty dash_mm, same colour (Registration), weight (0.25 pt), offset (3 mm) and length (5 mm) as crop_marks: (110,-3)-(110,-8), (120,-3)-(120,-8) and the same below. Rendered with pdftoppm (scratchpad .../audit/out/pro-1.png): the top edge carries four indistinguishable ticks at x = 0, 110, 120, 230. That is precisely the mark pattern of two 110 x 178 cards imposed 2-up with a 10 mm gutter, so a guillotine operator who follows the marks cuts the spine out. The trade convention is dashed/dotted fold marks vs solid cut marks, and the project's own research notes say so: print-requirements.prepress.md section 2 ('fold marks for the two spine folds drawn the same way, dashed') and print-requirements.folding.md section 2 ('Dashed fold ticks vs solid crop marks'). Home profile is only half-fixed: the SVG from `--example layout_svg -- poche home_a4` shows each fold mark as a solid 5 mm tick (M110 -2 L110 -7, identical to the cut ticks) followed by a dashed tail of only 3 mm (M110 -8 L110 -11, dash 1/1 = two 1 mm dashes), while the doc of caption_areas (marks.rs:346-348) suggests printing 'cut on the solid marks, fold on the dashed ones' - which would tell a home user to cut along the first 5 mm of each fold mark. Mutant check: making the press fold ticks dashed is rejected by the two tests above, i.e. the tests enforce the non-conventional style. (Convention stated from domain knowledge and the repo's notes; WebSearch budget was exhausted so it could not be re-confirmed online.)
findings.suggested_fix: Stroke fold ticks with a dash pattern in both styles (e.g. Stroke::dashed(color, weight, [1.0, 1.0]); consider a 3 mm length so they also differ in size), and in MarkStyle::Guide make the whole fold mark dashed from the bleed edge to the reach instead of solid + tail. Update professional_fold_marks_are_solid..., check_fold_marks and the home test accordingly. Optionally expose a label anchor next to the fold marks so the composer can set i18n FoldHere/CutHere.

findings.title: [Domain gap] The duplex flip edge the layout assumes is neither exposed nor documented; with the print-dialog default (flip on long edge) a home-printed card has its inside upside-down and behind the wrong cover
findings.evidence: The panel mirroring itself is correct for the architecture's definition (sheet turned about its VERTICAL axis): by hand for poche on A4 landscape, the front cover occupies sheet x 153.5..263.5 on side 1, inside-front is drawn at sheet x 33.5..143.5 on side 2, and a turn about the vertical axis maps x -> 297 - x = 153.5..263.5, i.e. behind the front cover, upright. But on a landscape sheet the vertical axis is the SHORT edge, so this requires 'flip on short edge'. With 'flip on long edge' (the default duplex setting) the sheet turns about its horizontal axis: x is unchanged and y inverted, so inside-front lands behind the BACK cover and the whole inside is rotated 180 degrees relative to the outside. Because the spread is symmetric the trim boxes still coincide, so nothing looks wrong until the card is opened. The portrait fallback (page.rs:90-91) needs the opposite setting (long edge). `grep -rni 'short edge|long edge|duplex'` over crates/ and docs/architecture.md finds no place that records this; SheetPlacement exposes only `landscape`; home()'s doc promises 'both sides register when the sheet is turned over', which is true for the boxes but not for the content. Not a numeric bug, but ebc-layout is the only crate that knows which orientation was chosen. (Flip-edge semantics derived from first principles; WebSearch was unavailable.)
findings.suggested_fix: Add `pub enum DuplexFlip { ShortEdge, LongEdge }` and `SheetPlacement::duplex_flip()` (ShortEdge when `landscape`, LongEdge otherwise), document it on PrintProfile::home, CardFormat::inside and new_page, and have the composer print the instruction in a caption area (needs an ebc-i18n Msg). Add a test that pins landscape -> ShortEdge, portrait fallback -> LongEdge.

findings.title: [Domain/numeric] target_px, min_px and effective_ppi are off by float rounding on inch-based sizes: 6 in at 300 ppi 'needs' 1801 px and an exact 300 ppi scan is judged Low
findings.evidence: Recomputed in python3: 152.4/25.4*300 = 1800.0000000000002 -> ceil = 1801 (also 76.2 mm -> 901); 1800/(152.4/25.4) = 299.99999999999994 -> judge_ppi returns Low for a scan that is exactly on target; on a 0.01 mm grid from 50 to 300 mm, 65 of 25,001 sizes ask for one pixel too many at 300 ppi. Computing mm*ppi/25.4 instead gives 1800.0 / 300.0 in the same cases. The crate's own test cover_image_on_each_preset... hides this with a `>= target_ppi - 1.0` tolerance. Four sparring tests added during the audit fail on it (tests/spar_resolution.rs).
findings.suggested_fix: Compute `mm * ppi / MM_PER_INCH` (multiply before dividing) and take `ceil(v - 1e-9)`; compute effective_ppi as `px * MM_PER_INCH / mm`; compare in judge_ppi with a relative epsilon (e.g. ppi >= target * (1.0 - 1e-9)).

findings.title: [Domain] Home printable margin is 5 mm on every sheet, below the 6.35 mm (0.25 in) hardware margin common on Letter/inkjet printers that the project's own notes recommend
findings.evidence: profile.rs:347 itself says 'home printers need 3-6.35 mm' and picks 5; print-requirements.folding.md section 6 recommends 'Keep everything, marks included, inside a 6.35 mm safe frame'. With 5 mm, on Letter the dashed fold guide runs to 13.95 mm from the trim = 5.0 mm from the paper edge and caption_areas reach 5.5 mm from the edge, so their outer 0.85-1.35 mm is clipped on a 6.35 mm printer. The essential cut/fold ticks and the ruler are safe (they end >= 9 mm from the edge on A4). Scratch run: with printable_margin = 6.35 poche still fits A4 (reach 9.65 mm) and Letter (reach 12.6 mm); digest and A5 are rejected either way. The value comes from the brief, so this is a profile-value correction rather than an implementation bug.
findings.suggested_fix: Use 6.35 mm for home profiles (or at least for Sheet::Letter) and update the three tests that hard-code the 11 mm / 13.95 mm reach.

findings.title: [Contract deviation] Marks cannot be built from the contract's field list: two extra mandatory fields and no Default
findings.evidence: The contract lists Marks { crop, fold, registration, color_bar, offset, length, weight_pt }. The struct adds `style: MarkStyle` and `scale_ruler: bool`, derives no Default and is not #[non_exhaustive], so a sibling crate writing the literal from architecture.md does not compile and has no `..Default::default()` to fall back on (only `..Marks::press()`). All other contract names (CardFormat and its presets/custom/spread/outside/inside/fold_x, SPINE_DEFAULT_MM, Panels, Sheet, PrintProfile fields, professional_eu, home, new_page, marks, safe_rect, Fit, place_image) are present with the promised signatures; the EBC.* Info keys match what ebc-preflight parses (meta.rs:477-538, 0.1 mm tolerance).
findings.suggested_fix: `impl Default for Marks` (= Marks::press()) and mention the two extra fields in architecture.md section 5 so sibling briefs use `..Default::default()`.

overall:
The crate is solid on the numbers, but three major problems remain, two of them not mentioned in the implementer's report.

**What holds up**
- **Contract names:** every promised name and signature is present and usable, except the `Marks` literal (minor).
- **Sheet sizes:** A4 210x297, Letter 215.9x279.4, A3 297x420 and SRA3 320x450 are correct.
- **Crop marks:** they lie on the extensions of the trim edges, start at max(offset, bleed), are 5 mm long at 0.25 pt, and never put ink in the bleed box.
- **Colour:** registration colour is used only for press-style strokes; home marks are black-only grey; the colour bar and guides are plain CMYK. There is no RGB anywhere.
- **Home margins:** home marks stay inside the printable area of the true sheet. The spread is centred, with 33.5/16 mm margins on A4 and 24.7/18.95 mm on Letter, so the tight margins fall on the printer's side margins.
- **Mirroring:** inside-front on the left is correct for a sheet turned about its vertical axis.
- **Report accuracy:** build, clippy, fmt, wasm, doc and test-count claims all reproduce. The tests are strong: 19 of my own mutants were all killed.

**What needs fixing before this ships**
1. **Home MediaBox is not the sheet (contract deviation, acknowledged by the implementer).** `pdfinfo` shows 262 x 210 mm instead of A4 for poche. Front/back registration then depends on the viewer centring an off-size page. The fix needs an explicit media box in `ebc_scene::Page` and `ebc-pdf`; `ebc-layout` already computes the sheet rect. The crate's tests currently pin the deviation.
2. **Fold marks are solid ticks identical to crop marks (domain error, not in the report's deviations).** On the press profile the top edge reads 0 / 110 / 120 / 230, exactly like a 2-up with a 10 mm gutter, so a finisher following the marks would cut the spine out. The project's own research notes call for dashed fold marks. The home variant is solid for its first 5 mm, with only a 3 mm dashed tail on A4.
3. **The duplex flip edge is not exposed or documented (domain gap, not in the report).** The layout is right only for "flip on short edge" on a landscape sheet, and "long edge" for the portrait fallback. The print-dialog default gives an upside-down inside behind the wrong cover.

**Minor**
- Float rounding in `target_px` / `effective_ppi`: 6 in at 300 ppi gives 1801 px, and an exact 300 ppi scan is judged Low.
- The 5 mm home printable margin is below the 6.35 mm common on Letter printers.
- `Marks` has two extra mandatory fields and no `Default`.

Other agents added sparring test files to `crates/ebc-layout/tests` during the audit; six of those tests currently fail, on item 1 and on the float issue.
